name: Sky Network Television Limited
sector: Communication Services / Media & Entertainment (Pay-TV, Streaming, Broadcasting)
overview: Sky Network Television is New Zealand's dominant pay-TV, sports-rights aggregator and, since 1 August 2025, free-to-air broadcaster, operating a satellite pay-TV service (Sky Box), streaming products (Neon entertainment, Sky Sport Now, Sky Go), a small broadband ISP, a commercial/hospitality distribution business (Sky Venue/Business), and, following the near-nil-cost acquisition of Discovery NZ (renamed Sky Free), the free-to-air channels Three/Eden/Rush/HGTV and the ThreeNow BVOD streaming platform. The core business is built around exclusive New Zealand and international sports rights (All Blacks/Super Rugby to 2030, NZ Cricket to 2032, NRL to 2034, Premier League to 2034, Olympics to Brisbane 2032) monetised across a linear satellite base in structural decline and a growing streaming/digital/advertising base. FY2026 (year to 30 June 2026) delivered underlying revenue of $826.1m (+9%) and underlying EBITDA of $157.0m (+6%), with reported NPAT of $59.8m (+190%, flattered by a $31.4m non-cash gain on bargain purchase from the Discovery NZ acquisition); the company holds a net cash balance sheet ($79.1m cash, no debt) and paid a fully imputed dividend of 32 cps for FY2026, with 10% p.a. dividend growth targeted through FY29 and a move to quarterly dividend payments from FY27.

business_model.summary: Sky earns subscription revenue from three delivery platforms carrying largely the same premium sport/entertainment content library (satellite Sky Box, streaming Neon/Sky Sport Now, and now free-to-air Three/ThreeNow), plus advertising sold across linear FTA, pay-TV, and digital inventory, a small broadband ISP, and commercial/hospitality distribution (Sky Venue, ~6,000 premises). Historically almost entirely subscription-funded, the Discovery NZ acquisition materially increases the advertising revenue mix (now 16% of total revenue, up from 8% a year ago) and gives Sky a genuinely 'free' consumer proposition for the first time, diversifying away from a satellite base that has been shrinking for a decade. Content is largely 'pass-through' from global studios/sports bodies (multi-studio strategy including Paramount, Sony Pictures Television, NBCUniversal, BBC Studios, StudioCanal) but is increasingly supplemented with locally commissioned Sky NZ Originals content and Sky-built channels (Sky Drama, Sky Kids, Sky Comedy). Management's stated FY31 ambition is to grow revenue significantly with 20-30% of revenue from non-subscription sources (advertising, other), a fundamental shift from a pure-subscription to an audience/advertising-diversified model.

revenue_streams.name: Sky Box (satellite pay-TV subscriptions)
revenue_streams.note: $446.5m of $826.1m FY2026 underlying revenue (54%, down from 62% a year ago as the base is diluted by Sky Free/advertising growth); Sky Box customers fell from 514,982 (FY2023) to 422,000 (FY2026), but annualised churn improved to 10.2% (lowest since FY22) and the rate of decline is slowing as the New Sky Experience (NSE) rollout (41% of base) improves retention

revenue_streams.name: Streaming subscriptions (Neon, Sky Sport Now, Sky Go)
revenue_streams.note: $128.3m FY2026 (+8%); Sky Sport Now grew 13% to $76.3m (159,000 customers, +9%) on price rises and a new Premium Pass; Neon rebounded strongly in H2 FY26 (+17% half-on-half) to 252,000 customers, only fractionally below FY25's 259,000, after falling to 215,000 in H1 following the non-renewal of exclusive HBO Max — the earlier 'Neon in structural decline' narrative did not hold through FY26

revenue_streams.name: Advertising (linear + digital)
revenue_streams.note: $131.7m FY2026, +131% YoY, driven by 11 months of Sky Free ownership ($77.2m contribution) plus modest Sky Standalone growth; 22% of ad revenue now digital (+113% YoY for Sky Standalone digital); broadcast/linear market share more than doubled to 35.2% post-acquisition

revenue_streams.name: Sky Free (Three, Eden, Rush, HGTV, ThreeNow) - from 1 Aug 2025
revenue_streams.note: Contributed 11 months in FY26; delivered $8.0m of Group synergies in year one (above the multi-year $10m+ by FY28 target pace) and was cash-flow positive for the year; management's FY27 priority is further optimisation and synergy delivery

revenue_streams.name: Broadband subscriptions
revenue_streams.note: $47.4m FY2026 (+28% YoY) off a small base; 59,000 customers (+15%); small but fast-growing bundling/retention tool, with 11-14% of Sky Box customers now bundling broadband

revenue_streams.name: Venue/Commercial (hotels, hospitality)
revenue_streams.note: $52.8m FY2026, down 2% YoY, serving ~6,000 hotel/hospitality/retail premises; sector pressure in accommodation/retail outpacing licensed-premises growth

business_model.customer_type: B2C mass-market residential (satellite, streaming, broadband, FTA) plus B2B commercial/hospitality (Sky Venue) and B2B advertisers/sponsors
business_model.geographic_mix: 100% New Zealand (Aotearoa NZ-focused strategy); NZD functional currency but material USD/AUD content and capex exposure (studios, sports rights, satellite)

main_competitors: HBO Max (standalone in NZ from 16 June 2026)
Warner Bros. Discovery (former content partner, now also a direct competitor)
DAZN (rights bidder, historically explored by NZ Rugby)
competitive_position.market_position: New Zealand's largest aggregator of premium sport and pay entertainment, and, since August 2025, also owns a free-to-air network (Three) and BVOD platform (ThreeNow), giving it reach across virtually every screen and price point in the country; broadcast/linear advertising market share more than doubled to 35.2% post-acquisition.

moat_factors.factor: Exclusive/anchor NZ sports rights, now materially extended
moat_factors.description: Long-dated exclusive deals across nearly every major code: NZ Rugby/SANZAAR to December 2030 (~$75-80m/yr, down ~30% from prior ~$111m/yr), NZ Cricket to 2032, Premier League extended a further 6 years to 2034, Olympics extended to Brisbane 2032, and a new exclusive 7-year NRL/Warriors deal to 2034 (~NZ$61m/yr, subject to shareholder approval) covering Sky Sport, Sky Sport Now, Three, ThreeNow and Sky Venue outlets. Staggered renewal dates reduce simultaneous negotiating risk and this content remains largely unavailable elsewhere in NZ.

Only provider with satellite coverage of NZ combined with streaming and, now, free-to-air; the NRL deal explicitly leverages this by distributing across paid and free platforms simultaneously — useful for both content partners maximising audience and advertisers wanting full-funnel reach

Unified Sky/Sky Free sales team from H2 FY26; advertising revenue +131% YoY; digital advertising now 22% of ad revenue and growing well ahead of the broader NZ digital video market (113% Sky Standalone digital growth vs 27% market growth); NZ digital ad spend $3.0bn (2025, +12%) is a large addressable pool

Net cash position ($79.1m cash at 30 June 2026, up 144% YoY, no debt), unlike most global streamers still burning cash; allows Sky to fund long-dated rights renewals (Premier League, NRL) and a 10% p.a. dividend growth target while still considering a buyback after FY27 interim results

35+ year history as NZ's default sport/entertainment aggregator; new Sky Experience hardware and rebranded Neon (new identity launched May 2026) are improving NPS (+11pts, three-year target +19pts) and churn, but brand recovery from 2025 satellite migration disruption and past price increases is still in progress

weaknesses: No content ownership at scale — Sky is fundamentally a rights aggregator/reseller dependent on renewing expensive contracts with NZR, NZC, NRL, Premier League, studios, etc., each a renewal/repricing risk, though recent renewals (Rugby, NRL, EPL, Olympics) reduce near-term risk through the early 2030s

Satellite technology remains structurally challenged versus IP-delivered streaming, requiring costly hardware (Sky Box/Pod), field technicians, and single-satellite dependency risk (evidenced by the 2025 Optus D2-to-KT6 migration disruption)
Small absolute scale (NZ-only, ~5m population) versus global streamers' content budgets amortised across hundreds of millions of subscribers

Sky Free/Three was a loss-making, declining, indebted business under Warner Bros. Discovery ownership for years; while year-one integration delivered $8.0m of synergies and cash-flow positivity, full optimisation and revenue-growth proof points are still to come in FY27
Venue/commercial segment revenue declining (-2% FY26) on soft accommodation/retail sector conditions

growth_drivers: FY31 growth ambition: management targets significant revenue growth with 20-30% of revenue from non-subscription sources by FY31, underpinned by a shift from 'products and subscribers' thinking to an audience/data/technology-led ecosystem model

Discovery NZ/Sky Free integration: year-one synergies of $8.0m already delivered (ahead of the pace needed for the at-least-$10m-by-FY28 target), with further optimisation flagged as a core FY27 priority as the businesses fully unify

Advertising diversification: digital advertising now 22% of ad revenue and growing far faster (113% YoY Sky Standalone) than the broader NZ digital video ad market (27% YoY), supported by dynamic ad insertion technology across Sky Sport Now, Sky Go and the new Sky Box
Broadband cross-sell: fast-growing (59,000 customers, +28% revenue FY26) via bundling with Sky Box, a retention tool against Spark/One NZ

New Sky Experience (NSE) migration: 41% of Sky Box base converted by FY26 (from 21% in FY25), improving reliability, NPS and lowering churn (10.2%, lowest since FY22) — accelerating uptake is an explicit FY27 priority

Long-dated sports rights locked in on materially improved/rational economics: NZ Rugby to 2030 (~30% cheaper), NZ Cricket to 2032, Premier League to 2034, Olympics to Brisbane 2032, and pending NRL to 2034 (~$61m/yr) — securing the content moat through the early 2030s while supporting the 47-49% programming-cost-to-revenue target (FY26 actual 47.3%, within range)

10% p.a. dividend growth targeted FY27-FY29, move to quarterly dividend payments from FY27, and a stated intention to consider an on-market share buyback or special dividend after FY27 interim results, subject to no superior use of capital

business.description: Sky Box customers fell from 514,982 (FY2023) to 422,000 (FY2026); satellite still 54% of group revenue. Decline has decelerated (churn improved to 10.2%, the lowest since FY22) as NSE rollout progresses, but the base is still shrinking every period and remains the largest single revenue line

business.risk: Sports rights renewal/loss and cost risk
business.description: The single largest content cost and revenue anchor is sport. NZ Rugby was retained in 2025 at a ~30% lower annual fee (~$75-80m vs ~$111m) after NZR reportedly explored DAZN as an alternative, and on a co-exclusive (not fully exclusive) basis with TVNZ taking provincial rugby. The pending NRL deal (~$61m/yr to 2034) is described as a 'record' deal and requires shareholder approval; any future loss of a marquee code to a global streamer (Amazon, DAZN) remains a long-term tail risk even though near-term renewal risk across major codes has now been substantially reduced through 2030-2034

business.risk: Sky Free/Discovery NZ integration and turnaround risk
business.description: Year-one integration was successful (operationally/culturally unified, $8.0m synergies, cash-flow positive), but the acquired business had a history of losses and declining linear advertising under WBD ownership, and further optimisation work continues through FY27; full realisation of the at-least-$10m-by-FY28 synergy target and durable revenue growth from the combined entity remain to be proven
Sky Venue revenue fell 2% in FY26 on softer accommodation and retail sector conditions outpacing growth in licensed premises

The 2025 Optus D2-to-KoreaSat6 migration caused significant customer disruption and reputational damage (subsequently compensated by Optus); illustrates ongoing single-satellite dependency risk until the base fully migrates to IP-hybrid technology

financial.description: Sky hedges USD/AUD exposure on programming rights, capex and lease costs via forward FX contracts, but a weaker NZD raises effective content costs against the 47-49%-of-revenue target, and large USD-denominated rights commitments (Premier League, NRL, Olympics) increase the multi-year FX exposure

financial.risk: Statutory earnings distorted by one-off items
financial.description: FY2026 statutory NPAT of $59.8m (+190%) is heavily flattered by the non-cash $31.4m gain on bargain purchase (Discovery NZ) plus Optus compensation, net of Sky Free integration/transaction costs and accelerated content amortisation; underlying NPAT growth of only 1.8% ($41.8m vs $41.1m) is the more representative run-rate figure and investors reading headline statutory profit will overstate underlying earnings power

FY26 dividend of 32 cps equated to 74.9% of normalised free cash flow, near the top of the stated 60-90% payout policy range; continuing 10% p.a. dividend growth while also funding rights renewals, integration costs and any buyback will require sustained FCF growth

regulatory.risk: Fair Digital News Bargaining Bill / media policy
regulatory.description: Government progressing a revised news bargaining code aimed at Google/Meta paying NZ news publishers; likely benefits TVNZ/NZME more directly than Sky, but the Three/ThreeNow FTA business brings Sky more directly into NZ media-policy and local-content-quota debates
Sky content is regulated under both the Broadcasting Standards Code and Commercial Video on Demand Code; the expanded FTA footprint (Three, Eden, Rush, HGTV) increases regulatory surface area

regulatory.risk: Shareholder approval risk on rights deals
regulatory.description: The new NRL rights agreement is explicitly stated as 'subject to shareholder approval,' introducing execution/approval risk to a strategically important content commitment

macro.risk: NZ recession / weak consumer and ad spend
macro.description: Management continues to flag 'challenging' trading conditions into H1 FY27 with 'economic recovery remains uncertain'; discretionary subscription products (Sky Box, Neon) and linear advertising remain directly exposed to household and corporate budget pressure

macro.risk: Structural advertising market decline offset by digital growth
macro.description: Total linear TV advertising market softness partly offset by strong digital ad growth (Sky's digital ad revenue growing far faster than the broader market); the FTA/BVOD business remains a bet that Sky can outperform a shrinking linear ad pool via digital/BVOD growth

macro.risk: Global content cost inflation / streamer consolidation
macro.description: Global SVOD players raising prices and consolidating as they seek profitability, which could flow through to higher content costs for Sky as a licensee under its multi-studio strategy (Paramount, Sony Pictures Television, NBCUniversal, BBC Studios, StudioCanal)

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global pay-TV in structural decline as IP/streaming displaces satellite/cable; NZ market specifically has seen Spark Sport exit live sports streaming, TVNZ+ scale as the free BVOD leader, and international SVOD (Netflix, Disney+, Amazon Prime, and now standalone HBO Max from June 2026) directly compete for entertainment subscription dollars. Sky's strategic response — becoming a genuine multi-platform (satellite + streaming + FTA + broadband) aggregator via the Discovery NZ acquisition, combined with long-dated exclusive sports rights across nearly every major code through 2030-2034 — is a direct bet that bundled reach, disciplined content economics, and locally-exclusive sports content can offset secular decline in any single platform while growing a materially larger advertising business.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderately cyclical — subscription and advertising revenue both correlate with NZ consumer/business confidence and discretionary spend; management has explicitly cited a multi-year NZ recession/weak-economy period (FY24-FY27) as a persistent headwind to both revenue lines, with 'economic recovery remains uncertain' language still used for H1 FY27
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct balance-sheet sensitivity given net cash position and no debt; moderate indirect sensitivity via NZ consumer discretionary spending and business/advertising confidence
key_input_costs: Sports and content broadcasting rights (NZR, NZC, NRL, Premier League, Olympics, studios)
Subscriber equipment (Sky Box/Pod hardware) and installation

recent_developments.event: Analyst consensus mixed: reported consensus price targets cluster around NZ$3.46 (range NZ$2.50-$4.00) against a share price near NZ$3.20-3.30; overall recommendation broadly a 'hold' to modest 'buy' lean among covering analysts

FY2026 full-year results released: reported revenue $824.8m (+10%), underlying revenue $826.1m (+9%); reported EBITDA $170.2m (+41%), underlying EBITDA $157.0m (+6%, near top of guidance); statutory NPAT $59.8m (+190%) boosted by $31.4m Discovery NZ bargain-purchase gain and $8.2m Optus compensation; underlying NPAT $41.8m (+2%); final dividend 17 cps, full-year dividend 32 cps (+45% YoY, 113% growth over 3 years, beating the FY23-set 'double to 30 cps' target a year ahead of plan); closing cash $79.1m (+144%), no debt

New multi-year strategic targets announced: FY31 ambition to grow revenue significantly with 20-30% of revenue from non-subscription sources; 10% p.a. dividend growth target FY27-FY29; move to quarterly dividend payments starting December 2026; capital allocation policy formalised at 60-90% of normalised free cash flow to dividends, with potential buyback/special dividend consideration after FY27 interim results; tighter capex envelope of 6-8% of revenue (down from 7-9%)

Secured an exclusive 7-year New Zealand NRL broadcast rights deal (2028-2034) with the Australian Rugby League Commission, reported at approximately NZ$61m/year, covering NRL, NRLW, all Warriors matches, finals and State of Origin, distributed across Sky Sport, Sky Sport Now, Three, ThreeNow and Sky Venue — subject to shareholder approval; also announced a 6-year Premier League extension through to 2034 and Olympic rights extended to Brisbane 2032

Warner Bros. Discovery launched HBO Max as a standalone streaming service in New Zealand, following Sky's decision (announced Feb 2026) not to renew exclusive HBO Max distribution rights — a direct new competitor to Neon; Sky responded with an expanded Paramount content partnership (Yellowstone spin-offs Dutton Ranch, The Madison, Y: Marshals) and a broader multi-studio strategy (Sony Pictures Television, NBCUniversal, BBC Studios, StudioCanal)

Neon relaunched with a new brand identity; customer base rebounded 17% half-on-half in H2 FY26 to 252,000 (from 215,000 in H1), delivering five consecutive months of growth and closing the year only fractionally below FY25's 259,000

H1 FY2026 interim results: underlying revenue $415.4m (+8%), underlying EBITDA $78.2m (+29%), underlying NPAT $19.3m (+77%); interim dividend 15.0 cps (+76.5% YoY); FY26 guidance narrowed to revenue $820-835m, EBITDA $145-160m, capex $62-68m, dividend at least 30 cps (subsequently beaten on all metrics)

Completed acquisition of Discovery NZ Limited (Three, Eden, Rush, HGTV, ThreeNow) from Warner Bros. Discovery for nominal consideration ($1 share price), debt-free, resulting in a $31.4m accounting gain on bargain purchase; renamed Sky Free

Announced new 5-year (through December 2030) NZ Rugby/SANZAAR broadcast rights deal at approximately NZ$75-80m/year versus ~NZ$111m/year previously (~30% cost reduction), retaining exclusive All Blacks/Black Ferns/Super Rugby rights while TVNZ became the free-to-air partner for provincial rugby

Completed accelerated 'Project Migrate' satellite transition from the end-of-life Optus D2 satellite to KoreaSat6, following service disruption for some customers; subsequently received compensation from Optus

guidance.as_of: FY2026 Annual Results / Results Presentation (28 August 2026)

items.notes: Reflects revenue expectations, continued Sky Free synergy delivery, and disciplined cost base management
Within the newly lowered target range of 6-8% of revenue (down from the prior 7-9% target, which was achieved at 7.2% consolidated in FY26)

items.vs_prior: new long-range target introduced at FY26 results
items.notes: Detailed 5-year strategic plan to be finalised as management's first FY27 priority; underpinned by a shift from 'products/subscribers' to an audience/data/technology-led ecosystem model, continued margin expansion and a tighter 6-8% of revenue capex envelope

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Sophie Moloney's three FY27 priorities: (1) finalise the strategic plan through FY31, (2) optimise the expanded business by unlocking further value from the Sky/Sky Free combination (targeting the at-least-$10m FY28 synergy goal), and (3) accelerate New Sky Experience uptake among the Sky Box base. Management continues to flag 'trading conditions continue to be challenging' into H1 FY27 with 'economic recovery remains uncertain,' while expressing confidence in the FY31 growth ambition, underpinned by long-term sports rights now secured across nearly every major code through 2030-2034, a flexible multi-studio entertainment strategy, and demonstrated ability to drive margin and free cash flow growth even through a weak economy and a major technology/business integration.

bull_case: Net-cash balance sheet (no debt, $79.1m cash) with a fully imputed, fast-growing dividend (15 cps FY23 to 32 cps FY26, +113% in three years, with a new 10% p.a. growth target through FY29 and quarterly payments from December 2026) makes this a credible income/yield stock, with explicit buyback/special-dividend optionality flagged for after FY27 interim results

The Discovery NZ acquisition was effectively free (nominal $1 consideration, debt-free) and is delivering ahead of plan — $8.0m of synergies in year one alone versus an at-least-$10m-by-FY28 target — while materially diversifying revenue into advertising (now 16% of total, +131% YoY) and digital, and more than doubling Sky's linear ad market share to 35.2%

The sports rights moat has been substantially de-risked and extended through the early-to-mid 2030s across nearly every major code (Rugby to 2030, Cricket to 2032, Olympics to Brisbane 2032, Premier League to 2034, pending NRL to 2034) on improved/rational economics (NZR ~30% cheaper), directly supporting the achieved 47-49% programming-cost-to-revenue target and structural EBITDA margin improvement (19.7% FY25 to 21-22% FY26)

Neon's H2 FY26 rebound (+17% half-on-half, five consecutive months of growth) alongside 13% growth in Sky Sport Now shows the streaming arm has stabilised and re-accelerated after the HBO Max non-renewal, undermining the bear thesis that streaming was also going into terminal decline

FY31 growth ambition (significant revenue growth, 20-30% non-subscription revenue mix, continued margin expansion within a tighter 6-8% capex envelope) gives a credible multi-year framework for re-rating if delivered, following three consecutive years of largely met or exceeded three-year targets
bear_case: The core satellite subscriber base continues to shrink every reporting period (Sky Box customers down from ~515,000 in FY23 to 422,000 in FY26) and remains 54% of group revenue; while churn has improved, the structural pressure from IP-delivered global streaming has not reversed

Statutory FY2026 profit growth is heavily flattered by one-off, non-cash items (bargain-purchase gain, Optus compensation); underlying NPAT growth of just 1.8% for FY26 is a far more modest true earnings trajectory than the headline 190% statutory profit growth suggests, and the dividend payout ratio (74.9% of normalised FCF) is already near the top of the stated 60-90% policy band, limiting headroom without FCF growth

Sky Free/Three was a loss-making, structurally declining linear FTA business under Warner Bros. Discovery for years; while year-one integration executed well, full realisation of synergies and durable advertising/audience growth in a still-shrinking linear ad market remains to be proven through FY27 and beyond

Management continues to describe trading conditions as 'challenging' with 'economic recovery remains uncertain' into H1 FY27 — a fourth consecutive year of a weak New Zealand macro backdrop weighing on discretionary subscription and advertising spend, with no clear inflection point yet visible

The pending NRL rights deal (~$61m/year to 2034) requires shareholder approval and, combined with the Premier League extension to 2034 and other long-dated commitments, materially increases Sky's forward content cost base and FX exposure at a time when the 47-49% programming-cost target has only just been achieved and any renewed cost pressure could compress the still-below-long-run-average EBITDA margin
